subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (SL), (IMC)(c) and (RU). (REP) is the exact frozen statement of cmc_exists_massRepresentation: a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U has a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, and an a.e. strongly measurable field ξ with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α and T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ (plus a null-set clause not used here). (SL) is the exact frozen statement of cmc_slice_mass_bounds: for open U, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) represented by (μ, ξ) and ∂T by (μ', ξ') (measures finite on compact subsets of U, a.e. strongly measurable fields, a.e. bounded by 1 in the coefficient norm) and L-Lipschitz f, there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) for open W, and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a<f<b}). (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity. (RU) is the frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq: if, in an open U ⊆ ℝ^P, three pairs (μ_i, ξ_i) (Borel measures finite on compact subsets of U, a.e. strongly measurable k-vector fields with |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.) satisfy ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then ∫_Bξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫_Bξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫_Bξ₃(ω)dμ₃ for every Borel B and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let d, P ∈ ℕ and T, Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) such that T, ∂T, Y and ∂Y have locally finite mass (M_W < ∞ for every open W with compact closure). If T and Y have the integer slice property, then so does T − Y. Here a current X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has the integer slice property (ISP) if for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X in ℝ^P (Borel measures finite on every compact set; a.e. strongly measurable fields of (d+1)- resp. d-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for a.e. x and every covector α, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm; X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂X(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms) and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, every pair A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity (the predicate written out verbatim in the frozen statements of the siblings cbr_slice_property_of_weak_limit and cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 7 (V4(o)). The slice currents T⌞{f<t}, (∂T)⌞{f<t}, Y⌞{f<t}, (∂Y)⌞{f<t} of the parent's step 0(i) are obtained here from (SL), which asserts their existence. Notation: E_t := {f < t}.
1. Representations. Apply (REP) with U := ℝ^P to T, ∂T, Y and ∂Y (they have locally finite mass). This gives (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) with measures finite on compact sets, a.e. strongly measurable fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x (hence a.e.), and T(ω) = ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T, ∂T(η) = ∫ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T}, Y(ω) = ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y, ∂Y(η) = ∫ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}. These are admissible representations in the sense of the integer slice property.
2. Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of T − Y and ∂(T − Y), and let f be L-Lipschitz; E_t is Borel for every t because f is continuous.
3. The integer slice property of T, applied to (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f, L, gives a null set N_T such that for t ∉ N_T every pair of currents satisfying the slice formulas for these representations has integer multiplicity ∂A − B; likewise the property of Y gives a null set N_Y. N := N_T ∪ N_Y is null.
4. (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, applied to T with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f, L (its hypotheses hold by step 1), gives currents A^T_t, B^T_t with A^T_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T and B^T_t(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T} for every t; likewise (SL) applied to Y gives A^Y_t, B^Y_t.
5. Linearity of restrictions. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = T(ω) = (T − Y)(ω) + Y(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ + ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y. Hence (RU) (k := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, triples (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ, ξ), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), whose hypotheses hold by step 1 and admissibility) with B := E_t gives ∫_{E_t}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ + ∫_{E_t}ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y. For every η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ∂T(η) = T(dη) = (T − Y)(dη) + Y(dη) = ∂(T − Y)(η) + ∂Y(η), so (RU) with k := d and the triples (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ', ξ'), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) gives ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T} = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' + ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}.
6. Fix t ∉ N and currents A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. By step 5, A(ω) = A^T_t(ω) − A^Y_t(ω) and B(η) = B^T_t(η) − B^Y_t(η). Hence for every η, (∂A − B)(η) = A(dη) − B(η) = [A^T_t(dη) − B^T_t(η)] − [A^Y_t(dη) − B^Y_t(η)], i.e. ∂A − B = (∂A^T_t − B^T_t) − (∂A^Y_t − B^Y_t) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
7. By step 3, applied to the pairs (A^T_t, B^T_t) and (A^Y_t, B^Y_t), both brackets are integer multiplicity, so ∂A − B is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c). Since N is null and (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ'), f were arbitrary, T − Y has the integer slice property. ∎
proof_key_steps: (REP) gives admissible representations of T, ∂T, Y, ∂Y; the integer slice properties of T and Y apply to them outside a null set.
(SL) provides slice currents of T and of Y for every t.
(RU) turns T = (T − Y) + Y and ∂T = ∂(T − Y) + ∂Y into the same identities for integrals over {f < t}.
Hence ∂A − B = (∂A^T_t − B^T_t) − (∂A^Y_t − B^Y_t), which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c).

audit.reason: REP and SL provide the required representations and restriction currents. RU proves both restriction identities, yielding the exact difference of slices outside a common null set. The stated IM difference hypothesis completes the proof without circularity.
